entries.provision: Ranex defines its core domain as governed deterministic execution rather than the agent loop.
A new dependency-clean kernel is built beside Hermes.
Workflow semantics and the execution reducer are first-class kernel responsibilities.
Hermes is contained as a replaceable worker and evolves into a typed action-proposal driver.
One fail-closed capability bus mediates every effect.
Policy enforcement, evidence and gate semantics, permit authority, module governance, and atomic event/outbox state remain kernel-owned.
Required capabilities ship as qualified first-party modules in one product release.
Legacy Hermes plugins execute only behind a constrained compatibility boundary.
Ranex starts with a small SQLite-backed tracer and retains a workflow-runtime port.
Import and runtime fitness tests enforce the architecture.

Remove the Nous commercial model provider and all account, credit, subscription, payment, entitlement, Portal, and promotional infrastructure; retain only provider-neutral cost and budget measurement.
`ranex.*.domain` cannot import Hermes, CLI, gateway, database, provider, filesystem, HTTP, or tool packages.
A bounded context imports another context only through its public API.
First-party modules may depend on application/kernel public APIs, but the kernel cannot depend on modules.
Domain and application code do not import adapters; the composition root alone constructs them.
The module dependency graph is acyclic and equals a checked-in manifest.
Importing any module is side-effect free.
No direct canonical-state writes occur outside the unit of work.
No external effect occurs without a capability grant and recorded activity identity.
The module catalog cannot override a permit issuer or policy enforcement point.
A disabled, incompatible, unqualified, or quarantined module cannot register, migrate, receive traffic, or perform an effect.
Only the execution kernel chooses a legal next canonical state.
Only nonreplaceable application control authorizes and dispatches capabilities and effects using domain authorization decisions.
Every target-mode effect is completely mediated and no special agent-tool bypass exists.
Policy or checker unavailability and error deny a blocking action.
A maker cannot approve its own subject.
Evidence and approval bind the exact project, run, packet, commits, workflow version, and policy activation.
An approval or permit is single-use, scoped, expiring, and invalidated by material change.
Canonical state and version, audit or domain record, permit consumption, and outbox intent commit atomically.
Every retry uses the same logical idempotency identity.
The reducer has no hidden nondeterministic dependency.
Replay of the same definition, version, and history yields the same state and commands.
Historical decisions remain explainable and new effects use fresh authority.
Module code cannot write canonical state or grant itself capability.
External plugin failure cannot weaken a gate.
A human waiver remains visible as a waiver and never becomes machine PASS.

Any legacy migration reader must be standalone and time-bounded, may recognize old Nous provider/account fields only to warn, redact, or translate a user to an explicit BYOK provider, must not be imported by normal startup, and cannot refresh a token or contact a Portal.

Legacy `$HERMES_HOME/auth.json` entries (`providers.nous`, `credential_pool.nous`, `active_provider="nous"`), shared `nous_auth.json`, and model/recommendation caches remain quarantined metadata. The reader reports “unsupported legacy provider,” offers explicit secret deletion, requires a new provider selection, and never silently moves an OAuth token into Ranex.
Payment methods, subscriptions, balances, entitlements, and billing authorization data are never copied into Ranex.
Preserve license, copyright, provenance, and required upstream attribution. Rebranding does not authorize erasing legal notices or Git history.

Remove Hermes/Nous branding from all Ranex product surfaces and, as separately checkable items, from package metadata; remote endpoints; headers; telemetry tags; help text; screenshots; generated assets; and defaults. Historical research citations and legally required attribution are exceptions.
A clean-host Ranex run makes no DNS or HTTP request to a Nous, Portal, or Nous inference host.
nous, nous-portal, and nousresearch do not resolve as a runtime provider or model-catalog owner.
`/topup` and `/subscription` commands, billing and subscription RPCs, checkout, card, and auto-reload schemas, and Portal proxy routes are unregistered.
Runtime packages exclude `x-nous-credits-*`, `billing:manage`, `providers.nous`, Portal OAuth scopes, managed tool-pool entitlement, and `product=hermes-agent` request tags.
A remote model catalog cannot introduce or activate a model outside the release-pinned Ranex catalog and qualification record.
Sessions, canonical databases, exports, and backups contain no payment method, subscription, commercial balance, Portal entitlement, or Nous auth token.
The wheel, container, and SBOM exclude dedicated billing UI, purchase clients, Nous provider plugins, generated billing bundles, and monetization-only dependencies.
Static and runtime route-census tests find no hidden import, command, hook, RPC, environment variable, URL, or feature flag that can reactivate the commercial subsystem.
A configured tool without direct credentials becomes unavailable and never attempts a Nous managed gateway or checks a commercial subscription.
An auxiliary or model fallback never selects Nous when the configured provider is missing or fails; missing configuration fails closed.
Legacy auth and config loading remains quarantined and cannot load a token, refresh credentials, log in, mint a key, or send network traffic.
Fuzzed `x-nous-*` headers cannot create state, notices, prompt content, tier selection, or tool gating.
Built wheel, npm bundle, and container scans find no dedicated commercial file, generated billing bundle, provider plugin, or `@nous-research/ui` package.
Provider-neutral token, cost, and budget telemetry continues to work after commercial deletion.
License and attribution verification passes.

No product-facing package name, CLI command, config root, header, telemetry tag, help screen, screenshot, generated asset, or default presents Hermes/Nous branding outside an explicit migration warning or legally required attribution.
The clean kernel contains a shared-identity facility that provides shared identity and a canonical-serialization facility that provides canonical serialization.
The clean kernel contains an Execution aggregate, and every Execution state transition is computed by its pure reducer.
The clean kernel persists canonical execution state and its associated version in relational storage.
The clean kernel contains an append-only transition and audit journal and an outbox, and persists them with canonical execution state and version through one SQLite unit of work.
The clean kernel permits event sourcing only for the Execution aggregate and only if its replay and migration tests justify that choice; every other module remains outside that event-sourcing scope.
The clean kernel contains an application-control policy-enforcement point that is fail-closed, uses pure domain decisions, and invokes a simple deterministic policy adapter.
Architecture import tests are part of the clean-kernel contract and must be present and passing before feature code is admitted.
The clean-kernel gate advances only when reducer replay tests and crash-boundary tests pass and the tested kernel has no Hermes import.

entries.decision_subject: Canonical Ranex workflow and event schema and upcaster policy.
Whether the local runner passes the required crash and recovery tests or a mature durable runtime is justified.
Exact transaction ownership across execution, evidence, permit, and work projections.
Atlas supported-language coverage and the conditions that produce UNKNOWN.
Dynamic parallelism, map or fan-out, and compensation semantics.
Whether and how hot module activation is allowed while executions are running.
State migration and rollback for active module versions.
Secure external-extension protocol and capability vocabulary.
Policy authoring language, including typed Python or JSON rules versus OPA or Cedar.
Reviewer independence and calibrated model-judge thresholds.
Host isolation profile and acceptable performance.
How much inherited Hermes session and search behavior Ranex retains.
Whether Kanban is a projection of canonical state or selected tables are adapted behind work management.
Whether a future release qualifies an independently hosted open-weight model originally published by Nous through a provider-neutral catalog.
Whether an unrelated third-party payment-system tool belongs in Ranex product scope and risk policy.
Whether voice becomes an explicit requirement and therefore permits a separately qualified TTS or STT delivery adapter.
Whether Electron and desktop bootstrap applications remain after selection of the local web or TUI product path.
Whether an existing-user transition requires a time-bounded hermes CLI migration shim.
Whether execution, gate, permit, and effect intent are submodules of one strong-consistency Governed Execution context or independently persistent contexts.
Whether to activate event sourcing for the Execution aggregate after its replay and migration tests justify that choice; the decision cannot authorize event sourcing for any other module.

entries.reason: The pinned-source audit and scorecard are historical evidence about Hermes 0.19.0, not Ranex runtime obligations.
The reusable-seam assessments guide characterization and extraction, but each retained asset still needs exact-version qualification.
The research explicitly labels the execution-state sketch illustrative and not the canonical enum.
The suggested layout is a research map; ADR-0007 now owns the exact canonical repository topology.
Exact upstream file deletion and salvage rows are pinned-revision migration inputs; the promoted release gates check outcomes without assuming those paths still exist.
The broad first-release profile list mixes accepted exclusions with conditional product-scope candidates and cannot be promoted as one blanket rule.
Archive and source-removal candidates depend on compatibility windows and parity evidence that do not yet exist.
The Phase 0 and Phase 0A freeze, characterization, and commercial-removal activities remain migration planning; the owner explicitly removed Phase 1 lines 1899-1912 from this disposition.
The validation inventory is a test-design source; exact executable fixtures require an enacted runtime subject and are not fabricated by the documentation validator.
Maturity labels and rejected foundations are advisory assessment; the genuine choices are separately registered as OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED.
Limitations, HY3 execution facts, and reviewer-model maturity are provenance and evidence, not deterministic Ranex authority.
Deferred capabilities and remove-from-core guidance do not authorize source deletion or activation; later scope ADRs and module contracts govern them.
Phases 2 through 6 remain implementation planning in this revision; the owner decision promoting Phase 1 does not silently promote their sequencing or exit schedules.
